_note: Invented satirical comedy. None of these incidents is historical; no quote is attributed to a real person; the brand's origin is not placed in any era.

chapters.title: I. The Prehistoric Bush
beats: Before history had a name, man lived alongside nature.
Gerald, however, had taken this relationship rather too far.
Three squirrels had moved into his undergrowth.
They had established a thriving community.

chapters.title: II. The Egyptian Experiment
beats: In ancient Egypt, personal appearance became a matter of royal importance.
Every detail was attended to with extraordinary care.

chapters.title: III. The Greek Question
beats: The Greeks were devoted to the pursuit of knowledge.
They questioned existence, nature, and the human condition.
But one mystery proved especially persistent.
A bold new theory was proposed.

chapters.title: IV. The Roman Empire
beats: The Romans mastered engineering on an extraordinary scale.
They built roads, aqueducts, and remarkable bathing facilities.
Yet certain provinces remained poorly maintained.
The Senate agreed to address the problem.

chapters.title: V. Medieval Armour
beats: In the Middle Ages, a knight's armour was his pride.
Every surface was kept in magnificent condition.
But beneath the polished steel lay a neglected frontier.
The blacksmith was summoned for an inspection.

chapters.title: VI. A Renaissance Invention
beats: The Renaissance brought a revolution in invention.
One visionary designed a remarkable solution.
Forty-seven gears. Six levers. One ambitious purpose.

chapters.title: VII. The Victorian Cover-Up
beats: The Victorian gentleman valued dignity above all things.
Certain subjects, however, were considered unmentionable.
Until one brave servant suggested a solution.

chapters.title: VIII. The Electric Age
beats: But the instructions left certain questions unanswered.
Some areas were still considered beyond the manufacturer's imagination.

chapters.title: IX. The Space Age
beats: Soon, mankind was reaching beyond the Earth.
An entirely new frontier had opened.
Every detail had been planned with scientific precision.

chapters.title: X. The Modern Age
beats: And so, after thousands of years of questionable decisions,
mankind finally found a better way to trim.
The kings rejoiced. The philosophers approved.
The squirrels, however, sought legal advice.
